entries.title: Acts 21:1
segments: When we had torn ourselves away and had set sail, we ran before the wind to Cos; the next day we came to Rhodes, and from there to Patara,

entries.title: Acts 21:2
segments: Where we found a ship crossing to Phoenicia, and went on board and set sail.

entries.title: Acts 21:3
segments: After sighting Cyprus and leaving it on the left, we sailed to Syria, and put into Tyre, where the ship was to discharge her cargo.

entries.title: Acts 21:4
segments: There we found the disciples and stayed a week with them. Speaking under the influence of the Spirit, they warned Paul not to set foot in Jerusalem.

entries.title: Acts 21:5
segments: However, when we had come to the end of our visit, we went on our way, all the disciples with their wives and children escorting us out of the city. We knelt down on the beach, and prayed,

entries.title: Acts 21:6
segments: And then said good-bye to one another; after which we went on board, and they returned home.

entries.title: Acts 21:7
segments: After we had made the run from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, and exchanged greetings with the Brethren there, and spent a day with them.

entries.title: Acts 21:8
segments: The next day we left, and reached Caesarea, where we went to the house of Philip, the Missionary, who was one of 'the Seven,' and stayed with him.

entries.title: Acts 21:9
segments: He had four unmarried daughters, who had the gift of prophecy.

entries.title: Acts 21:10
segments: During our visit, which lasted several days, a Prophet, named Agabus, came down from Judea.

entries.title: Acts 21:11
segments: He came to see us, and, taking Paul's girdle, and binding his own feet and hands with it, said: "This is what the Holy Spirit says--'The man to whom this girdle belongs will be bound like this at Jerusalem by the Jews, and they will give him up to the Gentiles'."

entries.title: Acts 21:12
segments: When we heard that, we and the people of the place began to entreat Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.

entries.title: Acts 21:13
segments: It was then that Paul made the reply: "Why are you weeping and breaking my heart like this? For my part, I am ready not only to be bound, but even to suffer death at Jerusalem for the Name of the Lord Jesus."

entries.title: Acts 21:14
segments: So, as he would not be persuaded, we said no more to him, only adding--"The Lord's will be done."

entries.title: Acts 21:15
segments: At the end of our visit, we made our preparations, and started on our way up to Jerusalem.

entries.title: Acts 21:16
segments: Some of the disciples from Caesarea went with us, and brought Mnason with them, a Cypriot disciple of long standing, with whom we were to stay.

entries.title: Acts 21:17
segments: On our arrival at Jerusalem, the Brethren there gave us a hearty welcome;

entries.title: Acts 21:18
segments: And the next day Paul went with us to see James, and all the Officers of the Church were present.

entries.title: Acts 21:19
segments: After greeting them, Paul related in detail all that God had done among the Gentiles through his efforts;

entries.title: Acts 21:20
segments: And, when they had heard it, they began praising God, and said to Paul: "You see, Brother, that the Jews who have become believers in Christ may be numbered by tens of thousands, and they are all naturally earnest in upholding the Jewish Law.

entries.title: Acts 21:21
segments: Now they have heard it said about you, that you teach all Jews in foreign countries to forsake Moses, for you tell them not to circumcise their children or even to observe Jewish customs.

entries.title: Acts 21:22
segments: Well now, as they are certain to hear of your arrival, do what we are going to suggest.

entries.title: Acts 21:23
segments: We have four men here, who have of their own accord put themselves under a vow.

entries.title: Acts 21:24
segments: Join these men, share their purification, and bear their expenses, so that they may shave their heads; and then all will see that there is no truth in what they have been told about you, but that, on the contrary, you yourself rule your life in obedience to the Jewish Law.

entries.title: Acts 21:25
segments: As to the Gentiles who have become believers in Christ, we have sent our decision that they should avoid food offered to idols, and blood, and the flesh of strangled animals, and impurity."

entries.title: Acts 21:26
segments: On this, Paul joined the men, and the next day shared their purification, and went into the Temple, and gave notice of the expiration of the period of purification when the usual offering should have been made on behalf of each of them.

entries.title: Acts 21:27
segments: But, just as the seven days were drawing to a close, the Jews from Roman Asia caught sight of Paul in the Temple, and caused great excitement among all the people present, by seizing Paul and shouting:

entries.title: Acts 21:28
segments: "Men of Israel! help! This is the man who teaches every one everywhere against our People, our Law, and this Place; and, what is more, he has actually brought Greeks into the Temple and defiled this sacred place."

entries.title: Acts 21:29
segments: (For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in Paul's company in the city, and were under the belief that Paul had taken him into the Temple.)

entries.title: Acts 21:30
segments: The whole city was stirred, and the people quickly collected, seized Paul, and dragged him out of the Temple, when the doors were immediately shut.

entries.title: Acts 21:31
segments: They were bent upon killing him, when it was reported to the Officer commanding the garrison, that all Jerusalem was in commotion.

entries.title: Acts 21:32
segments: He instantly got together some officers and men, and charged down upon the crowd, who, when they saw the Commanding Officer and his men, stopped beating Paul.

entries.title: Acts 21:33
segments: Then he went up to Paul, arrested him, ordered him to be doubly chained, and proceeded to inquire who he was, and what he had been doing.

entries.title: Acts 21:34
segments: Some of the crowd said one thing, and some another; and, as he could get no definite reply on account of the uproar, he ordered Paul to be taken into the barracks.

entries.title: Acts 21:35
segments: When Paul reached the steps, he was actually being carried by the soldiers, owing to the violence of the mob;

entries.title: Acts 21:36
segments: For the people were following in a mass, shouting out: "Kill him!"

entries.title: Acts 21:37
segments: Just as he was about to be taken into the Fort, Paul said to the Commanding Officer: "May I speak to you?" "Do you know Greek?" asked the Commanding Officer.

entries.title: Acts 21:38
segments: "Are not you, then, the Egyptian who some time ago raised an insurrection and led the four thousand Bandits out into the Wilderness?"

entries.title: Acts 21:39
segments: "No," said Paul, "I am a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of a city of some note; and I beg you to give me permission to speak to the people."

entries.title: Acts 21:40
